title: Pricing request routing and cost-allocation decision tree
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We receive frequent non-bug customer requests related to commitments, invoicing mechanics, cost allocation across teams, and marketplace billing flows. Currently intake happens via support tickets, SDR notes, and ad-hoc emails. Decision latency and inconsistent routing cause escalations, duplicate work, and incorrect commercial commitments.

Objective: Create a pragmatic, operational decision tree and routing playbook to triage pricing/packaging/billing requests at intake. The output must: 
- Standardize required intake fields so requests are actionable by finance, sales ops, or product without back-and-forth.
- Define a prioritization heuristic based on revenue impact, contract status, compliance risk, and product complexity.
- Provide deterministic routing rules (who owns: Sales Ops, Finance, PM, Customer Success, Legal) and SLA targets for initial response and resolution.
- Include example templates for responses, escalation paths, and required artifacts (e.g., draft SOW, sample invoices, cost models).

Scope: Commitments (reserved capacity discounts and contract terms), invoicing exceptions and timing, cost allocation tags/usage splits, marketplace billing disputes, and requests for contract amendments related to pricing.

Out-of-scope: One-off pricing experiments run by Growth without enterprise commitment, engineering feature requests unrelated to billing mechanics, and tactical refunds under $500 (handled by Support).
intake_form_fields: Request type (commitment | invoice | cost-allocation | marketplace | other)
Contract start/end and existing commitment (if any)
Supporting artifacts (contract PDFs, billing statements, sample invoices)
triage_matrix: Priority scoring: revenue_impact (0-5) + compliance_risk (0-5) + operational_complexity (0-5) + customer_tier_weight (1 for PLG, 2 mid-market, 3 enterprise)
High priority (score >= 10): immediate routing to Sales Ops + Finance + PM; SLA initial response 24h; resolution target 7 business days or defined contract milestone
Medium priority (score 6-9): route to Sales Ops + CSM; SLA initial response 48h; resolution target 15 business days
Low priority (score <=5): route to Product Backlog / Growth; SLA acknowledge 72h; resolution in next pricing review cycle
routing_rules: If request_type == commitments => owner: Sales Ops (primary), Finance (review), Legal if terms change
If request_type == invoice and dispute_amount > $5k => owner: Finance (primary), CSM informed
If cost-allocation and involves multi-tenant split => owner: Product + Sales Ops; require technical feasibility assessment (ENG-2412)
If marketplace billing (third-party fees, attribution disagreements) => owner: Marketplace Ops + Finance; escalate to Legal for TOS changes
If security/compliance flag set => immediate Legal + Security review
sla_targets: Initial triage acknowledgement: Enterprise requests within 24 hours
Routing decision made and owners assigned: 48 hours for high-priority; 72 hours for medium/low
Resolution targets: 7 business days (high), 15 business days (medium), next pricing cadence (low)
required_artifacts: Signed contract or draft amendment for commitments
Copy of invoice and payment trace for invoicing disputes
Example usage reports and tagging schema for cost allocation requests
Marketplace transaction logs and fee breakdowns for marketplace issues
decision_authority: Discounts or pricing concessions up to $25k ARR: Sales Ops (with Sales Manager approval)
Commitment term changes beyond standard tiers: Finance + Head of Revenue approval
Legal or TOS changes affecting marketplace terms: Legal Director sign-off
Engineering-scope changes affecting SKU or metering: Eng manager + Product
example_workflows: Example: Enterprise requests a 20% committed discount. Intake via form -> score=12 -> route Sales Ops + Finance -> Sales Ops drafts amendment + Finance validates cost model -> Legal reviews terms -> Sales Manager signs -> Sales Ops communicates to CSM and Finance updates billing system

Example: Customer disputes a marketplace fee. Intake -> route to Marketplace Ops -> Marketplace Ops pulls transaction logs, confirms fee origin -> if merchant misattribution, Marketplace Ops issues adjustment and Finance triggers credit memo
acceptance_criteria: A one-page decision tree diagram and one-pager playbook published to Confluence
A standardized intake form created in Zendesk with required fields and automated routing rules
Routing automation rules implemented in Support ops (work with RevOps) for top 4 request types
SLA monitoring dashboard tile added to Redwood Console (commercial-ops dashboard)
At least two runbook-tested examples completed end-to-end with cross-functional signoff
tasks: Interview top 8 customers and Sales reps to surface common request patterns - owner: Liam (due 2025-02-20)
Draft intake form fields and validation rules - owner: PM team (due 2025-02-14)
Design decision-tree diagram and one-pager - owner: Design (DES-2643) (due 2025-02-21)
Implement Zendesk form and routing automation with RevOps - owner: RevOps (due 2025-02-27)
Create SLA monitoring tile in Console - owner: ENG + Observability (dependent ENG-3120) (due 2025-03-05)
Run two pilot triages with active customers and capture lessons learned - owner: CSM + PM (due 2025-03-01)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly rigid routing causing false positives -> Mitigation: include an override workflow and weekly review by RevOps
Risk: Missing required artifacts from requesters -> Mitigation: make fields required in Zendesk and auto-request attachments on submit
Risk: SLAs unrealistic if requests require legal review -> Mitigation: classify legal-needed items and surface a separate SLA with legal lead-time

notes: Implementation should be iterative: ship intake form + basic routing first, then add scoring and SLA dashboard in the next sprint
Keep PM, Finance, and Legal aligned on definition of "high revenue impact" — recommend setting AR threshold at $50k ARR for 2025 initial rollout
Consider automating common safe approvals (e.g., standard commitment tiers) to reduce manual workload
